points.note: Small chain sprocket mounted coaxially in front of the large brass crank drive gear at platen level; chain visibly wraps it and descends to the crank. Axle bore + retaining pin clearly visible and used as the dead-center point.

Second sprocket, at the crank's own pivot on top of the green cylindrical post; identified by cross-reference with ch11_images/page002_img03.jpeg and page002_img04.jpeg ('fiducial mark' pivot boss on the crank arm, matching sprocket+chain arrangement). Not the SPEC pinion target, added as permitted.

More-visible of two brass fluted rollers at the base, directly behind/below the pinion sprocket and crank drive gear, with fine parallel teeth visible above it matching the cylindrical (non-tapering) 'cylinder gear set' reference photos in ch13_images/page001_img01.jpeg and page002_img01.png. Center taken at the silver retaining pin visible in the mounting bracket that should coincide with the shaft axis; the true hub bore itself is largely covered by the black bracket, so this is an inferred axis point rather than a directly-seen bore.

Second, smaller brass disc immediately to the right of cylinder_gear_center_1, mostly in shadow and partly occluded by the green crank-axle post. Center is a rough estimate from the small visible arc of its rim; could plausibly be the cone gear instead of a second cylinder gear (see cone_gear_center in occluded) - end-on views of a tapered vs. uniform roller look identical, so this identification is uncertain.

occluded.reason: No tapered/conical gear profile is resolvable anywhere in this front elevation. End-on, a cone gear's cross-section looks identical to a cylinder gear's (both are circular), and this straight-on front view gives no side-length view of any roller to detect tapering, so the cone gear set (ch12_images reference) cannot be confidently located or distinguished from the two brass discs marked as cylinder_gear_center_1/2. It may be one of those two discs, or fully hidden behind the platen carriage / crank drive gear.

The rocker-arm fan (ch14_images reference) is mounted directly below/behind the black platen recording box; from this straight front elevation the entire fan is hidden behind the platen box and its rack, with no blade edges peeking out at the box's sides.
